resolution: Diagnosed the stairs/terrain inconsistency as two missing laws, both in framework physics. (1) Placed props with baked collision triangles (the white stairs prop) resolve through the exact mesh-triangle lane, and that lane had NO step-height concept: projectedTrianglePush in framework/game/mesh_collision.zig treated a 0.2m stair riser exactly like a 10m wall, pushing the player centre a radius off the riser plane so the step-up mount (a point sample at the centre) could never reach the tread — which is why cranking step height to 2.0 changed nothing. Proc stairs climb because they decompose to plain boxes, and the box lane has grace_walkable/too_tall_to_step. Fix: a steep face topping out at/below feet+step_height is now skipped by the push — the mount law seats the feet — mirroring the box law; also inverse-scaled the world-metre tuning distances for scaled props. (2) Terrain cliffs read walkable because heightfieldSurface smeared the gradient over a ±1-cell central difference: a rise inside one cell reported HALF its grade, so at walk_cos 0.6 a ~69° wall passed the walkability gate and the too-steep move-cancel never fired. Fix: sample at ±half-cell so a one-cell cliff reads its true grade while sub-cell sculpt noise stays averaged. Added tests: staircase walk mounts to the top platform, a 2m face still walls, a one-cell 2.5m cliff reads normal_y<walk_cos. zig build test-game-mesh-collision all green; test-game-physics 53/54 with only the documented pre-existing hollow-ramp red. Framework change — needs the dev host binary rebuilt to take effect.
